newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker raps SEC inaction on 2000 computer bug.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker raps SEC inaction on 2000 computer bug.

text.p: The top Democrat on the House Commerce Committee said on Wednesday that he is concerned by the lack of progress by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the securities industry in tackling the so-called millennium computer bug.
"While there appears to be a high level of awareness and activity, the lack of progress in many areas is troubling," said John Dingell, a Michigan Democrat.
The lawmaker's comments were in response to an SEC study undertaken at his request.

The problem arises from computer programs written in the 1970s and 1980s that read only the last two digits in a year. The 00 reading for 2000 would cause an error in some programs or could be interpreted as 1900.
The SEC said in the study that it is aware of potential problems and has made some progress and said the same of industry efforts.
The lawmaker called on the SEC to nail down specific problems in the industry.

"Sunlight being the best disinfectant, it may be time to 'name names,'" Dingell warned. "We have been advised that some major broker-dealers are behind other parts of the finanicial industry in addressing this problem."
Dingell called on the SEC to develop its own method for for evaluating industry precautions in order to "spot potential train wrecks."

In the study, the SEC noted that it's largest internal system, called EDGAR, is currently "2000 compliant." For the remaining 88 central systems, 55 perform critical functions and of those six are in order for the millennium, the study said.
However, 38 systems still need work, the SEC said.

Nonetheless, the agency said that it has found a "very high level of awareness" in the industry. But it warned that the high levels of awareness and responses underway "do not guarantee that the problem will be universally solved."
The agency cautioned that public companies and investment companies must disclose to investors potential millennium problems.
